rationale: Six sources now, and the 2026 additions supply the two cases the earlier three left open. The sign case is measured directly: with lenses attached densely enough to compare all six hookpoint types, detection and intervention rankings over components are negatively correlated at Spearman -0.43, MLP outputs showing the weakest detected toxic signal and producing the largest reduction when modified while MLP inputs do the reverse. The same paper adds a second-order warning -- the published attention-head result reproduces exactly and is still misleading, because the most effective targets were in components nobody had instrumented. The magnitude case: the canonical refusal direction predicts a steering vector's safety damage by cosine similarity and ablating it recovers at most about 8 points of mean attack success rate, leaving worst-case unchanged on two of three models, while a direction learned against the intervention's own objective goes below the unsteered baseline. And the gap is not a constant: computing an unembedding lens's prediction and the actual effect of steering for the same write direction gives agreement rising from about zero in layers 0-5 to 0.91 at the final layer, so it is widest exactly where most probing is done.
statement: How well a direction or signal detects a property licenses no claim about what intervening on it does — not the size of the effect, and not even its sign.
